rotary-dimmer.model: Single Color Mini Rotary Dimmer, 12-24 V DC PWM, with an on/off switch at the end of its turn, 2.1 mm plug in; its board taken out of the housing and screwed into the foot's pocket, the knob replaced by the acrylic one

moon-cord.model: Black textile-braided 3-core 0.75 mm2 pendant cord, 3 m (cut to the drop), a cord grip in the canopy and a strain relief in the cap, and a mounting strap for a 4 in junction box

north-driver-575.model: A Class 2 constant-current driver at about 175 mA, 22 to 30 V window, 120 V AC in, phase-cut dimmable, FCC Part 15 Class B (consumer), dimming to 10 % or below, PF 0.90 or more at its load (JA8): the Vero SE 10 at about 175 mA runs about 24.5 V, about 4.3 W, about 575 lm (scaled from DS120: the 350 mA row less 2 % efficacy gain at half current, an estimate). north-driver-010v.model: A 0-10 V dimmable Class 2 constant-current driver at 350 mA (Mean Well LCM-25 kind, its output current set by DIP switch): the bar option, where a venue runs 0-10 V dimming

_core: Round 35 (2026-10-22): Core, the Orb with its own battery (the owner: 'I want it to work plugged in or not. Why does it need a separate cartridge for that?'). Prices are estimates.

core-cells.maker: any reputable LiFePO4 maker (to qualify: A123/Lithium Werks, EVE, Lishen)
core-cells.model: Three LiFePO4 26650 cells (IFR26650), about 3,000 mAh at 3.2 V each, in parallel (1S3P): about 29 Wh; about 2,000 cycles to 80 % (several times ordinary Li-ion's 500 or so); each to IEC 62133-2 and UN 38.3 (a UN 38.3 test summary from the cell maker). Each cell about 9.6 Wh (at most 20 Wh) and the set about 29 Wh (at most 100 Wh): Core ships under the small-battery exception (49 CFR 173.185(c), UN3481, contained in equipment), not as fully regulated Class 9

core-holder.model: A moulded holder for three 26650 cells with spring contacts, keyed for polarity, its NTC against the cells, wired to the board

core-board.model: Core's board: a USB-C sink (5 V 3 A); a switching LiFePO4 charger with power path, Analog Devices LTC4162-F (synchronous step-down, 1 to 9 LFP cells, up to 3.2 A, I2C telemetry and termination: no trickle charge at rest, so the maintenance power stays low for the DOE battery-charger limits and Title 20); a charge limit at about 3.45 V (about 90 %) by default with a full-charge mode; a battery protector (over/under voltage, over current, short circuit) and a fuel gauge, charging held off below 0 C and above 45 C by the cells' NTC; the two-channel warm-dim LED driver (2200 to 2700 K, about 2.5 W) and the capacitive touch on the ring

core-foot.model: A silicone foot ring 117 x 114 x 2 (Shore 40, non-slip), and the hatch's O-ring

core-screws.model: Four captive M3 x 6 stainless pan-head screws (Phillips or Torx T10) with retaining washers, for the hatch

north-driver-pcd16.model: PCD-16-350A, constant current 350 mA, 24 to 48 V, 120 V AC in (the A type), phase-cut dimmable (TRIAC, leading and trailing edge), UL 8750 Class 2, 84 x 57 x 29.5: in the canopy. The Vero SE 10 at 350 mA runs 26.0 V typical (DS120), inside the window: about 9.1 W, about 1,100 lm at Tc 25 C (1,020 at Tc 85 C). The 1,100 lm level. Kept as the bar-only alternate: its datasheet lists FCC Part 18 non-consumer (A type), a risk for homes (Part 15 Class B)
north-driver-pcd16.note: The review's B1: the PCD-16-700B (16 to 24 V, 180 to 295 V in) could not light the COB. FCC Part 18 non-consumer per the review: confirm for home sales

south-heatpipe.maker: any (Wakefield, Advanced Thermal Solutions, Shenzhen makers)
south-heatpipe.model: A sintered copper-water heat pipe, 8 across, about 220 long: its evaporator in the hub (at the bottom: gravity returns the fluid, the easiest way round for a heat pipe), its condenser in the fins' core above the lid; rated about 30 W at that length, far over South's 4 to 8 W; set in thermal paste
